clue.text: Accepting knight was forthright about not much of value years ago

definitions.text: not much of value years ago

indicators.note: the jumbled phrase takes the knight in among its letters
the letters of 'was forthright' are turned about into a new order

parts.note: N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A plain-speaking knight holding forth about trifles in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was a quarter of an old British penny, so a farthingsworth is a tiny amount; 'years ago' marks it as dated.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthing's worth was the smallest amount of value you could buy with pre-decimal British coins.

clue.text: Former vice-president Gore, in support of prime minister, ultimately quits for a bit

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath

parts.note: to gore is to pierce with a horn; it loses its R to become PIECE
last letter of minister, which quits PIERCE

explanation.surface: A political roll call: Al Gore backing a prime minister before bowing out for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gore' looks like Al Gore beside 'vice-president', but the vice-president is Pence and gore is a verb. 'Prime minister' splits: prime is a number, minister supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit is a coin, as in a threepenny bit, and a five pence piece is a British coin.

clue.text: Bras: any different shades?

indicators.note: the letters of 'Bras any' are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A lingerie shopper asking whether the bras come in other colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shades' pretends to mean colours of underwear; it is slang for sunglasses, and Ray-Ban is the brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray-Bans are a well-known make of sunglasses, which are informally called shades.

clue.text: They time hotel covering bins for us

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
bins is British slang for spectacles

explanation.surface: A hotel keeping bins out of sight for its guests' sake.
explanation.walkthrough: Bins here are not rubbish containers but glasses, short for binoculars and extended to spectacles in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Hourglasses measure time by running sand from one bulb to the other.

clue.text: Put away novel when lecturer rings in recess

indicators.note: the lecturer goes round the novel
receding, the lecturer runs backwards

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer; backwards NOD
She, the novel by H. Rider Haggard, placed inside NOD

explanation.surface: Someone shelving a novel while a lecturer phones during the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is not N or new here but a specific book, Haggard's She. 'Put away' means eaten, in the sense of putting away a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is to eat it heartily, and noshed is informal for ate.

clue.text: Still angry after what's said when turning over similar card (spades)

parts.words: what's said when turning over similar card
parts.note: in the card game Snap you call 'Snap!' when two matching cards turn up
S for spades, as in bridge notation

explanation.surface: A card player still fuming after an opponent's call during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb but is a noun: a still photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, often one taken from a film, and a snapshot is a quick informal photograph: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Round edges on aircraft-carrier's propeller

indicators.note: take just the first and last letters of aircraft-carrier

explanation.surface: The rounded edges of the flight deck on an aircraft carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: A carrier's propeller suggests a ship's screw, but the answer is a much humbler way of pushing a boat along.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar propels a rowing boat, so it is a propeller.

clue.text: Flattered drag act in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the pieces are to be heard

explanation.surface: A drag performer flattering the judges at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag act' is one phrase in the surface, a cabaret turn, but splits into two words: pull and deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To toady is to flatter someone in a servile way.

clue.text: Child's hero battling for Spooner's journalism

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: Jack Reacher is Lee Child's hero; he takes the F sound from the next word
battling = fighting; it takes the R sound from Reacher

explanation.surface: A children's comic hero in a fight, reported by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' looks like a youngster, making the hero a comic-book figure; it is the thriller writer Lee Child, whose hero is Jack Reacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Feature writing is journalism of longer articles rather than news reports.

clue.text: They look very ordinary, of course, touring ancient city

indicators.note: a tourist goes round a place

parts.note: O = ordinary, as in O level
Ur of the Chaldees, placed inside YES

explanation.surface: Tourists who look quite ordinary on a trip round an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They look very ordinary' reads as a description; the definition is only 'They look', since voyeurs are watchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Voyeurs are people who watch others, so they look.

clue.text: Sky, swell broadcasting channel

parts.note: a swell is a wave on the sea

explanation.surface: An advert for the Sky satellite TV channel as swell.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster, which makes 'Sky' look like part of the definition; it is plain sky, the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airwave is the radio frequency used for broadcasting.

clue.text: Seed in training, finishing with ace

indicators.note: to finish with something is to end on it, so A comes last

explanation.surface: A seeded tennis player in practice, closing with an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is tennis: seeds, training, aces. Here the seed is the kind a plant grows from.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas are the edible seeds of a climbing plant, so a pea is a seed by example.

clue.text: Some actors put on this musical sketch

parts.note: to sketch or paint a picture

explanation.surface: Actors staging a comic sketch from a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks like staging a show; it means applying make-up. 'Some actors' because not all wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasepaint is stage make-up that actors put on their faces.

clue.text: Popping up close to shrub, otter ran off

indicators.note: the letters are sent off in a new order
take the last letter of shrub

explanation.surface: An otter popping up beside a bush and then running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popping up' reads as one phrase, but the definition is only 'Popping', as in popping eyes; 'up' joins the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Protuberant means bulging out, as popping eyes do.

clue.text: Jenny possibly visiting North American university city

indicators.note: a visitor is inside someone else's home

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey

explanation.surface: A woman called Jenny visiting a college town in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a woman's name; it is a female donkey, and 'possibly' flags it as an example of an ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas, so the bare word city defines it by example.

clue.text: I'm not surprised Motown singer's cancelled

parts.note: a cancelled event is off, a no-go; its letters open the answer

explanation.surface: A fan shrugging at news that Stevie Wonder's concert is off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'singer's cancelled' as 'Wonder is a no': Stevie Wonder, the Motown star, is off, and NO goes in front of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No wonder' is what you say when something is unsurprising.

clue.text: Mum home for a chat, maybe around one, fine and clear

parts.note: a chat is a small bird, like the stonechat; its home is a nest
F = fine, as on pencils; inside NEST

explanation.surface: Mum coming home for a chat at about one, on a fine clear day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home for a chat' looks like a visit to talk; the chat is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plain to see, or clear.

clue.text: Transport given the green light in Brussels, perhaps part-submarine

definitions.text: Transport given the green light in Brussels, perhaps part-submarine

parts.words: Transport given the green light in Brussels
parts.note: reads like EU regulators approving a transport scheme; really a train setting off from Brussels on a green signal
reads like a vehicle that half dives; really a train that runs partly under the sea, through the Channel Tunnel

explanation.surface: A vehicle project cleared by EU officials in Brussels, part submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eurostar train leaves Brussels on a green signal and runs partly under the sea through the Channel Tunnel; 'submarine' means under the sea, not a submersible boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the train linking Brussels and Paris with London via the Channel Tunnel.

clue.text: Coastal region's flower swathing Italy area

indicators.note: to swathe is to wrap in cloth

parts.note: a flower is something that flows: a river
I = Italy, the international vehicle code; inside RIVER

explanation.surface: A coastal flower wrapped round a patch of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the classic crossword trick: read it as flow-er, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A riviera is any sunny stretch of coast, named after the Italian and French Rivieras: a plain synonym for coastal region.

clue.text: Inclination behind lad reportedly causing optical phenomenon

indicators.note: to be behind is to follow
what is reported is passed on by word of mouth

parts.note: an inclination of the head is a bow

explanation.surface: A boy's head tilt somehow producing a trick of the light.
explanation.walkthrough: A sunbow is a rainbow made by sunlight on spray, as at a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbow is a rainbow-like arc of colour, an optical phenomenon.

clue.text: Ill in bed, daughter spilt fresh peach drink

indicators.note: the remaining letters are made new

explanation.surface: A sick daughter in bed knocking over a fresh peach drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the drink; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bellini is a cocktail of peach purée and prosecco.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with dad getting face lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting runs the word upwards

parts.note: puss is slang for face; upwards it is SSUP

explanation.surface: Refusing to have anything to do with a father who has had a facelift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face lifted' suggests cosmetic surgery; puss is old slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up a chance is to decline it, an idiom for having nothing to do with it.

clue.text: Check out wearing skimpy top and head for inn exit

parts.note: in = wearing, as in 'in a suit'
a vest is a sleeveless top

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of inn

parts.note: a gate is a way out

explanation.surface: A scantily dressed guest checking out and heading for the exit of an inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check out' belongs to the hotel scene but is the definition: examine.
explanation.definitionFit: Check out is the informal phrasal verb for examine, a plain synonym of investigate.

clue.text: Finales for tuneful couple, Minnelli and Garland

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Last numbers from the singing duo Liza Minnelli and Judy Garland, her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Garland looks like Judy Garland beside Minnelli; it is the definition, a garland of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Leis are the flower garlands hung round visitors' necks in Hawaii, a definition by example.

clue.text: Opening Bible book I see being read out in church

parts.note: CE = Church of England; it holds the rest
the letter C sounds like see

explanation.surface: A reading from the start of a Bible book in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the opening of a book, set by 'Bible book'; it is a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack in rock or a wall, so it is an opening: a plain synonym.

clue.text: What's physician essentially on about? Spleen

indicators.note: the essence, or middle letter, of physician

explanation.surface: A patient asking what the doctor is saying about their spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor makes spleen look like the organ; here it means bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means anger or ill temper, as in venting one's spleen.

clue.text: All quitting halfway through swampy hike, like Zanzibarian?

indicators.note: each of the next three words stops halfway, keeping its first half

explanation.surface: Giving up halfway through a swampy trek, as a Zanzibari might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' seems a link to the definition but is the third word to be halved. The question mark marks Zanzibarian as an example: Swahili is spoken in Zanzibar.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is the language and culture of the East African coast, including Zanzibar.

clue.text: Picking the best old volunteers, fast and smart to guard funds

indicators.note: a guard stands round what it protects

parts.note: the Territorial Army, the old name for Britain's volunteer reserve
to smart is to sting; it goes round POT

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest veteran volunteers, quick and clever enough to protect the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast and smart' read as adjectives, quick and clever; they are a noun, Lent, and a verb, sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent-spotting is identifying and picking the most gifted people.
